answer: Latency triangulation gives each agent a rough physical footprint: random verifier nodes ping it at unannounced moments, and the round-trip times must fit one plausible location. A farm running a thousand identities from one rack is like an orchard planted on a single terrace; every tree answers with the same timing signature, so they collapse into one reward share. Faking distinct places means renting real servers far apart, a cost that drains an attacker like water through karst.
